definitions.explanation: A band worn around the neck of a dog, cat, or other animal, often for identification or to attach a leash.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}に{首輪|くびわ}をつけた。
examples.english: I put a collar on the dog.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{首輪|くびわ}をした{猫|ねこ}を{見|み}かけた。
examples.english: I spotted a cat wearing a red collar.

examples.japanese: {首輪|くびわ}に{名前|なまえ}と{電話番号|でんわばんごう}が{書|か}いてあったので、{飼|か}い{主|ぬし}に{連絡|れんらく}できた。
examples.english: The collar had a name and phone number on it, so I was able to contact the owner.

notes:
Compound of {首|くび} (neck) + {輪|わ} (ring/band). Refers almost exclusively to animal collars in modern Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {首輪|くびわ}をつける: to put on a collar
- {首輪|くびわ}を{外|はず}す: to take off a collar
- {首輪|くびわ}をした{犬|いぬ}: a dog wearing a collar
- {首輪|くびわ}に{名札|なふだ}をつける: to attach a name tag to a collar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ネックレス: necklace (for people — jewelry)
- リード/{引|ひ}き{綱|づな}: leash (often attached to the {首輪|くびわ})
- ハーネス: harness (alternative to collar for dogs)

USAGE:
In modern Japanese, {首輪|くびわ} is not used for human jewelry. Saying someone has a {首輪|くびわ} metaphorically implies being controlled or restrained.
